interactionPlan.concept: The relationship between a discrete periodic box function's spatial width and its Fourier transform frequency representation.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand how the box half-width L affects the main lobe width of its Fourier transform.
The student will be able to explain the reciprocal relationship between spatial domain width and frequency domain localization (the uncertainty principle).
The student will understand how the repetition period N of the box function changes the spacing and density of the discrete spectral samples.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: As the box function becomes wider in the spatial domain, its spectral representation in the frequency domain becomes narrower and more concentrated—demonstrating the fundamental scaling property of the Fourier transform.

interactions.label: Box Half-Width (L)
interactions.effect: Dynamically widens or narrows the blue box pulses in the spatial domain stem plot, while simultaneously narrowing or widening the corresponding sinc-like envelope in the frequency domain plot.
interactions.teaches: Demonstrates the reciprocal relationship between spatial width and spectral bandwidth (wider spatial pulse results in a narrower frequency spectrum with more tightly packed zero-crossings).

interactions.label: Period (N)
interactions.effect: Adjusts the spacing between the periodic repetitions of the box function in the spatial domain and changes the number of discrete frequency samples under the spectral envelope.
interactions.teaches: Shows how periodic replication in time/space discretizes the continuous spectral envelope, with larger periods leading to denser spectral sampling.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: The demo should feature two side-by-side or stacked stem plots. The left plot (Spatial Domain) replicates the style of the provided image: a discrete stem plot with blue stems and solid blue circular markers, centered at 0 with periodic repetitions at multiples of N (e.g., -N, 0, N). Key ticks on the horizontal axis should dynamically update to show -N, -N/2, L, N/2, N. The right plot (Frequency Domain) shows the magnitude of the DFT of this signal as a stem plot, clearly tracing a $|\sin(x)/x|$ (sinc) envelope. The interactive elements should fluidly update both plots to visually reinforce the Fourier transform dualities.
